text: Which adipocyte-specific genes (single-cell) encode blood-secreted proteins and have no detectable mRNA in liver?
plan: Cell type category (scRNA): Adipocytes / Cell type enriched AND Secretome annotation: Secreted to blood AND Tissue category (RNA): Liver / Not detected
understanding: The question asks to identify genes that are specifically expressed in adipocytes according to single-cell RNA sequencing data, are classified as encoding proteins secreted to blood, and have no detectable mRNA expression in liver tissue.

trail.why: To identify adipocyte-specific genes in single-cell data, the level 1 cell type 'Adipocytes' must be paired with 'Cell type enriched', which designates genes with at least four-fold higher mRNA levels in that specific cell type compared to any other.
The question asks specifically for proteins secreted into the blood, matching the 'Secreted to blood' option under secretome annotation.
The 'Not detected' category for a selected tissue corresponds to genes with mRNA below the detection cut-off (no detectable mRNA) in liver.

requirements.why: It defines RNA specificity across individual cell types based on single-cell RNA-seq, matching the requested 'adipocyte-specific' criterion at single-cell resolution.
It categorizes predicted secreted proteins by destination, including 'Secreted to blood'.
It classifies RNA expression and specificity (including not detected categories) across tissues including liver based on consensus RNA-seq data.
